answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task reveals fraud. A beacon selects the samples unpredictably, so an attacker cannot cheaply prepare only the identities likely to be checked; a reef of independent reviewers confirms each result before penalties apply. A raven may still create many accounts, but each must lock real capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it—making Sybils costly rather than impossible.
